title: Thread-decomposer foundational body architecture
scope: Foundational body-and-feeding architecture of the K6 thread-decomposer kingdom at qualitative grain, selected as an Author custom combination of the displayed weaver and bloom options; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: Thread decomposers are macroscopic, non-photosynthesising heterotrophs feeding through thread-form bodies.
They are distinct from microbial life; the Lineage II digestive symbionts remain separate microorganisms.
They are the planet's primary macroscopic decomposer-recycler kingdom.
Their ordinary state is diffuse feeding threads living hidden in soil, litter, and dead material.
On locating concentrated dead material, threads consolidate it into wrapped, felted masses that decompose from within, leaving spent husks.
Reproduction erupts episodically in fruiting structures keyed to wet and thaw windows.
Where thread decomposers are absent or fail, dead material can persist abnormally long.
Mutualist partnerships with producer kingdoms remain a bounded branch possibility, not the kingdom default.
boundaries: Thread, weaver, wrapped mass, felt, husk, and fruiting structure are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
The architecture establishes no Earth fungus, mycelium, mould, or mushroom homology.
Species, thread and mass anatomy, chemistry, digestion, wrapping thresholds, consolidation pacing, and mass sizes remain open.
Wrapping concentrated finds is the working pattern, not a guarantee; finds can be missed, contested, abandoned, or too dispersed, and no decomposition rate is established.
Fruiting structure forms, cues, seasonality, dispersal, toxicity, and edibility remain open; episodic eruption establishes no fixed calendar.
Abnormal persistence of dead material where the kingdom fails is a tendency, not a preservation guarantee; other decay paths remain possible and open.
Spent felts and husks are candidate materials only; no harvest, craft, product, or human use is established.
Producer partnerships, parasitic branches, predatory branches, and any living-tissue feeding remain open possibilities requiring their own records.
No thread-decomposer member is established as present, dominant, or absent at any particular location.
Earth and mythological inspiration remains author-facing; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted.

Mana patterns remain open; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, spawn point, refill node, guaranteed harvest, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Moisture, temperature, energy, nutrients, substrate, time, disturbance, and competition remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: Scenes can show wrapped and felted deadfall in every stage of consumption, husk shells, and seasonal fruiting eruptions.
Tell-tale preserved dead material can mark places where weavers are missing or failing.
Spent felts and husks stand as candidate materials for later culture records.
Every species, site, material use, and event requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The architecture describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, guaranteed resource, spawn source, refill node, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What thread and mass anatomy, chemistry, and digestion implement the architecture?
What thresholds and pacing govern wrapping and consolidation?
What fruiting forms, cues, and dispersal strategies exist, and which are toxic or edible?
Are felts and husks usable materials, and for what?
Which producer partnerships, parasitic branches, or predatory branches exist?
How do decomposition rates shape litter, casing, and carcass persistence across habitats?
sources: Author combination proposal and confirmation on 2026-08-17

author_approval.evidence: After the A/B/C cards were presented with A recommended, the Author proposed combining A and B ('A+B?'); the combined weaver-and-bloom model was presented and the Author confirmed 'Yes — record A+B' on 2026-08-17.
